review_notes:
I read the whole target file (lines 1–85), every downstream use of `closedUpperDisk`/`openUpperDisk` in the repository (DiskBoundaryRegion.lean, DiskSideRegionImages.lean, DiskTwoSideGlue.lean, DiskCrosscutHomeomorph.lean), the `diskDiameter_image`/`diskUpperArc_image` normal forms in DiskSemicircleGeometry.lean, and Mathlib's `Metric.mem_ball`, which is used for comparison.

The only simp-interface problem I found is that the two set definitions have no membership lemmas. Every proof that needs membership unfolds the definition by name and then calls `mem_ofPred`. The other lemmas in the file are topological facts (`_isClosed`, `_isOpen`, `_closure`, `_interior`, `_frontier`), and it is right that they are not simp lemmas.

I did not recommend `@[simp]` on `closedUpperDisk_eq`. It rewrites a named set into `closedBall ∩ imCLM ⁻¹' Ici 0`, which is a worse form for `simp` than the membership predicate. I also did not recommend `@[simp]` on `openUpperDisk_closure` or `closedUpperDisk_interior`. Downstream code uses them with `rw` on purpose, and they are not general normalisation rules.

I have not compiled anything. The claim that the proposed lemmas would close the listed goals with less unfolding rests on reading the goals, not on running Lean.

findings.excerpt:
def closedUpperDisk : Set ℂ := {z | ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ z.im}
def openUpperDisk : Set ℂ := {z | ‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im}
findings.problem: There are no membership lemmas for these two sets. Every proof that reasons about `z ∈ closedUpperDisk` or `z ∈ openUpperDisk` has to put the definition name into the simp set and then remove the set-builder with `mem_ofPred`. This happens in the target at line 19 (`simp [closedUpperDisk,mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right]`), line 33 (`simp [openUpperDisk,mem_ball,dist_zero_right]`) and line 59 (`simp only [mem_sdiff,closedUpperDisk,openUpperDisk,mem_ofPred,mem_union]`). The same pattern appears four more times in DiskBoundaryRegion.lean. As a result, the only way to simplify membership is to unfold the definition. That ties every caller to the literal `{z | ...}` form. Also, `simp [closedUpperDisk]` unfolds every occurrence of the constant in the goal, including occurrences that are not membership goals.
findings.proposed_change:
Add membership lemmas tagged `@[simp]` directly after the definitions, with the predicate in the same form the downstream proofs already reach:

@[simp] lemma mem_closedUpperDisk {z : ℂ} : z ∈ closedUpperDisk ↔ ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ z.im := Iff.rfl
@[simp] lemma mem_openUpperDisk {z : ℂ} : z ∈ openUpperDisk ↔ ‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im := Iff.rfl

Then replace `closedUpperDisk,…,mem_ofPred` and `openUpperDisk,…,mem_ofPred` in the `simp only` calls with these lemmas. In plain `simp` calls, drop the definition names from the simp set. Do the same for `openLowerDisk` and `closedLowerDisk` in DiskBoundaryRegion.lean.
findings.benefit: Each lemma's right side is a plain predicate on `‖z‖` and `z.im`, so the rule terminates and does not compete with any other rule. It matches the Mathlib convention for named sets, where `Metric.mem_ball` is a simp lemma and `ball` is not unfolded. Callers such as `conj_image_openUpperDisk`, `closed_halfDisks_union` and `closed_halfDisks_inter` could then be proved with `simp` or `simp only [mem_closedUpperDisk, …]` without depending on how the set is implemented. The definitions also stop being unfolded in places where only membership needs rewriting.
